item.title: Euronews' crew assaulted by masked individuals while covering protests in Paris
item.description: Euronews correspondents in Paris covering the protests reported being targeted by masked individuals on Saturday’s major nationwide demonstrations following calls on social media to target media outlets and professionals to prevent coverage.

item.title: Protesters storm town hall and clash with police in France’s Marseille
item.description: Protesters broke into Marseille town hall and clashed with police during nationwide demonstrations over rising prices in France.

item.title: 'We are here to help them,' says yellow vests representative on joining students for nationwide protests
item.description: Two separate major protests – one led by trade unions, the other by students – were initially slated to take place in Paris on Saturday. Eyewitnesses say the protests have converged into one massive demonstration demanding government remedies to the ongoing crises.

item.title: Tourism office set ablaze during cost-of-living protests in Lyon
item.description: A branch of Lyon’s tourist office was vandalised and set on fire during nationwide protests over rising prices in France.

item.title: Portugal sees protests over cost of living and housing crisis as demonstrations sweep Europe
item.description: It comes as major cost-of-living demonstrations in France on Saturday turned violent as protesters clashed with riot police.

item.title: Hungarian PM Péter Magyar says Zelenskyy unlikely to visit Budapest later this month
item.description: Zelenskyy's deputy chief of staff told Euronews earlier this week that the Ukrainian leader had been invited to Budapest on 23 October, to join events commemorating the 70th anniversary of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital following lung operation
item.description: The 71-year-old pontiff had been recovering in Rome's Gemelli hospital since undergoing a lung operation on Tuesday.

item.title: Super tanker ablaze after striking mine in Strait of Hormuz, IRGC says
item.description: The IRGC navy accused the tanker of having turned off its positioning and radar systems in an effort to evade detection.

item.title: North Korea says it tested new AI-powered torpedo system
item.description: It comes after North Korea tested two types of underwater-launched strategic cruise missiles on Wednesday as part of what is believed to be a push to bolster its naval capabilities.

item.title: No money for Ukraine and EU budget cuts: What could a Le Pen victory mean for the EU?
item.description: Le Pen is campaigning on a platform that would reshape France’s relationship with the EU ahead of the 2027 presidential election, potentially setting Paris on a collision course with Brussels with far-reaching implications.

item.title: Trump signs executive order waiving new Russia sanctions package
item.description: Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev has called the decision to put the sanctions on hold a "significant and truly historic moment."

item.title: Video shows Norwegian teenager arrested over UK contract killing plot
item.description: A Norwegian teenager who travelled to the UK to carry out a gangland killing has been sentenced to 20 years in detention.

item.title: Dozens arrested as protesters clash with security forces in Paris in major day of planned demonstrations
item.description: The French government stepped up security measures ahead of Saturday’s nationwide protests over the cost-of-living crisis, with student groups also expected to join demonstrations amid fears of potential clashes.

item.title: The world’s biggest fine jewellery factory: How Pandora aims to make more and pollute less in Vietnam
item.description: Pandora invested $150 million (€132mn) in a Vietnam factory, which it says will operate entirely on renewable electricity. The company also switched to using 100% recycled gold and silver in its jewellery production in 2024.

item.title: Trade unions push for EU law to address menopause at work
item.description: The European Trade Union Confederation wants menopause enshrined in EU workplace legislation, as the European Parliament examines the issue and the Commission stops short of proposing a dedicated strategy.

item.title: Smashing pumpkins: Annual squash festival draws thousands to Brussels castle
item.description: Organisers in Belgium expect 50,000 visitors at a pumpkin festival that will celebrate the wonderous ways of using the big vegetable.

item.title: Europe’s sponge cities are turning rain from waste into a valuable resource
item.description: The EU is creating a ‘Sponge Facility’ to help implement nature-based projects that aim to make cities less prone to droughts and floods.

item.title: Data centres are the new front line and Europe’s AI factories should slow down, says UN adviser
item.description: Data centres have become prime military targets and the drone strikes in Ukraine should force Europe to rethink where it builds its AI infrastructure, one expert says.

item.title: Trip designers, wellness and privacy: What's trending in luxury travel for 2027?
item.description: Next year, the luxury travel sector is set to be less about grand displays of opulence, and more about being intentional. From slower itineraries to privacy and dining experiences, here’s what the discerning traveller should know.

item.title: From fruit to bricks: Hong Kong engineers explore how to build houses on Mars
item.description: Engineers in Hong Kong are developing 3D-printable building materials that could one day be used to construct houses on Mars. Inspired by freeze-dried fruit, the team is combining sand, gelatine and genetically engineered yeast to create a concrete-like material under simulated Martian conditions.

item.title: Sanchez rejects criticism of Spain's migration policy: 'Words do not match reality'
item.description: Spain's prime minister defended the country's record on tackling irregular migration amid criticism of its mass regularisation plan, while Ursula von der Leyen called for full implementation of the EU migration and asylum pact.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV urges Putin to agree to truce in besieged Ukrainian city of Oleshky
item.description: The call took place at Rome's Gemelli Polyclinic, where the Pope is recovering well from surgery, on the same day he celebrated his first Mass since the operation.

item.title: Trump's new press secretary leaves after less than a week following controversy
item.description: Zacharia has long described herself as a lawyer while working as a commentator for conservative outlets such as Fox News and Newsmax.

item.title: Romanian president calls for greater NATO oversight in the Black Sea in Euronews interview
item.description: In an interview with Euronews, Romanian President Nicușor Dan warns that Black Sea security is under growing pressure as drone attacks hit commercial vessels off Romania and Bulgaria.

item.title: Budget, Ukraine, migration: Five takeaways from the EU leaders’ summit
item.description: EU leaders ended their Brussels summit with no deal on the budget, a new €70bn Ukraine funding gap, open clashes over energy and migration, but fresh resolve to create new trade defence tools to battle China.

item.title: Albanian PM blames 'foreign hands' for escalating anti-government unrest
item.description: Police said 160 people were detained following violent incidents on Thursday evening.

item.title: Global timekeeping rules change: leap second scrapped from 2027
item.description: Global timekeepers have voted to end the practice of adding extra seconds to UTC, citing risks to computer systems and the prospect of the first-ever negative leap second.

item.title: Commission and Ukraine launch joint task force over EU accession
item.description: The Commission and Ukraine launched a joint task force meeting twice a week to speed up accession reforms on the rule of law and anti-corruption, after Hungary lifted its veto and two more negotiating clusters were opened.

item.title: EU–Turkey summit in October aims to restart Cyprus talks
item.description: President Christodoulides said the high-level meeting would focus on resuming negotiations over Cyprus and advancing EU-Turkey relations.

item.title: Japan's first female PM says makeup and housework add hours to her working day
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi says household chores and getting ready for TV appearances add three to four hours to her working day compared with male predecessors.

item.title: Uzbekistan signs $4.7bn energy deals and outlines plans for two more nuclear power plants
item.description: Foreign firms including ACWA Power, EDF and Toyota Tsusho are involved in projects covering 3,000 MW of generating capacity and 400 MW of storage. Tashkent is also preparing 128 oil and gas exploration blocks for investors and pursuing a future electricity connection to Europe.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass as recovery from cancer surgery progresses
item.description: Vatican Media has released the first images of Pope Leo XIV since his hospitalisation, showing him celebrating Mass at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital as he recovers from lung cancer surgery.

item.title: Palestinians in Gaza dread another winter with nowhere safe to shelter
item.description: More than 44,000 people still live in buildings marked for demolition across the territory, unable to leave because no alternative shelter exists. Euronews spoke to families in Al-Mughraqa as tarpaulin prices double and Israel blocks timber and shelter kits from entering Gaza.

item.title: Belgium: Pumpkimania festival takes over Groot-Bijgaarden Castle
item.description: Foxes, owls and deer made from pumpkins have taken over Groot-Bijgaarden Castle near Brussels. The Pumpkimania festival features a 772kg giant, pumpkin boat rides and Halloween activities until 1 November.

item.title: Paris Motor Show: Renault and Citroën unveil electric concepts inspired by classic cars
item.description: Some of Europe's best-known cars are making a comeback at the Paris Motor Show, reinvented for the electric age.

item.title: '‘It’s easier dealing with Trump than Putin,’ Zelenskyy tells Euronews amid US tensions
item.description: After a week of tensions between Washington and Kyiv, Zelenskyy said Trump was still easier to deal with than Putin, despite the US president’s calls for new leadership in Ukraine and criticism of the Ukrainian leader.

item.title: Could Tesla’s flying car send sales and shares soaring?
item.description: Tesla revealed its next-generation Roadster on Thursday in Texas, with one of the three new versions performing a jaw-dropping kickflip and demonstrating flying capabilities. However, analysts contacted by Euronews Business do not expect the model to generate significant revenue.

item.title: Vatican releases first photos of Pope Leo XIV after lung tumour surgery
item.description: The Vatican has released the first images of Pope Leo XIV since he underwent surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung.

item.title: Norwegian teenager sentenced to 20 years in prison over UK murder plot
item.description: UK Counter Terrorism Policing said Natland had been operating under orders from someone in the Foxtrot Network, an international criminal gang based in Sweden.

item.title: This 19th-century Portuguese farmhouse in the Algarve is being transformed into a wellness retreat
item.description: Shanti-Som Algarve will offer six different programmes focusing on things like detoxing, relaxation, and burnout recovery.

item.title: From Samarkand to Paris: Preserving Central Asia's scientific heritage
item.description: From the scholars of the Silk Roads to new research institutions in Tashkent, Uzbekistan is seeking to make its historical legacy more accessible. Experts meeting at UNESCO headquarters in Paris examined its contribution to world civilisation and the value of shared cultural knowledge.

item.title: Inside Qatar’s Geekend where gamers, cosplayers and artists share their love of games, comics and anime
item.description: From anime costumes to locally designed board games, Geekend brings Qatar’s pop-culture fans together, with artists selling their work and gamers meeting face to face.

item.title: Russian missiles spark huge factory fires in Ukraine’s Odesa and Zaporizhzhia
item.description: Russian strikes ignited massive fires at businesses in Odesa and Zaporizhzhia as President Zelensky met European leaders for talks.

item.title: France and Germany strike car-industry deal linking 2035 engine rules to ‘Made in Europe’ push
item.description: Under the agreement, carmakers would be required to cut their CO₂ emissions by 90% by 2035, without having to offset the remaining 10%, as initially proposed by the Commission.

item.title: Ukrainian drones force closure of all four Moscow airports overnight, cancelling dozens of flights
item.description: Moscow’s airports were closed for 101 hours in the first 14 days of October, more than double the total for all of September.

item.title: Italy: Nationwide air traffic control issues disrupt flights at Rome airport
item.description: Flight delays and cancellations disrupted Rome’s Fiumicino Airport on Friday 16 October after a fault in the data-transmission network supporting Italy’s nationwide air traffic control system.
